metadata.title: Reproduction Package for ATVA 2021 Article `PJBDD: A BDD Library for Java and Multi-Threading'
metadata.description:
Reproduction Package

PJBDD: A BDD Library for Java and Multi-Threading

Abstract

This artifact is a reproduction package for the tool paper “PJBDD: A BDD Library for Java and Multi-Threading” (submitted to ATVA 2021).

It contains code and data used in the evaluation of the paper, including PJBDD with the implementation described in the paper the benchmark suite used for the evaluation, the raw data resulting from the evaluation, scripts to run the experiments, and instructions for reproducing the tables and figures in the paper.

A full reproduction of the evaluation requires 15 GB of memory, 8 CPU cores, and multiple weeks of CPU time. A limited subset of the benchmark tasks can be used for demonstration purposes if at least two CPU cores and 4 GB memory are available.

This artifact is published at Zenodo.

Content

This artifact contains the following items:

  • README.md: this documentation
  • License.txt: license information of the artifact
  • pjbdd: a directory containing PJBDD at revision master:58bd6889 which was used in our evaluation
  • packages: the necessary Ubuntu packages to run the experiments.
  • evaluation_results: raw data produced from our full experiments and scripts to create tex plots used in the paper
  • Makefile: a file to execute the commands

This Readme file will guide you through the following steps:

  1. Setup of PJBDD and BenchExec
  2. Performing demo experiments
  3. Analyzing the experimental data

TL;DR

Type the following commands to:

  • Install Java 11: make install-java-11 (please ignore warnings about an existing Java 8)
  • Install BenchExec:
    • $ make install-benchexec
    • reboot the system
    • $ make prepare-benchexec (to turn off swap memory and allow user namespaces, needs to be redone after every reboot)
    • $ make test-cgroup (to test if cgroup is configured correctly)
  • Test if BenchExec is installed successfully: $ make test-benchexec
  • Configure hardware requirements for the demo runs to X GB of memory and Y CPU cores: $ bash configureDemo.sh -m=X -c=Y

metadata.title: Reproduction Package for CAV 2021 Article `JavaSMT 3: Interacting with SMT Solvers in Java'
metadata.description:
This reproduction package contains the JavaSMT library, CPAchecker (internally using JavaSMT), benchmarks for evaluation, and the raw evaluation results for the article.

This replication package is intended to be used on Ubuntu 20.04.

The artifact directory contains a README that consists of five parts:

  1. Setup

  2. Example Task

  3. Performing the Evaluation

    1. Reproducing Table 4 from the Paper

    2. Reproducing Figure 2 from the Paper (Complete Set of Benchmark Tasks)

    3. Reproducing Figure 2 from the Paper (Smaller Subset of Benchmark Tasks)

    4. Executing the Complete Benchmark

  4. Data Analysis on our Raw Results

  5. Using JavaSMT as Library in an Application

The reproduction package has the following structure:

  • benchmarks:
    Benchmark definition files for the evaluation using BenchExec. Each file contains a series of benchmark tasks that are executed and measured when following the steps of this README.md. BenchExec creates HTML tables from the result data. The tasks reference source files from the directory sv-benchmarks. Our raw benchmark results are available in the directory results_raw.

  • cpachecker:
    A checkout of CPAchecker in the version used in the submitted manuscript. It is provided in a ready-to-run version and can be used for evaluation, both for single manual runs via a command line as well as for automated execution of multiple runs via a benchmark of BenchExec. CPAchecker contains the release 3.7.0-72-g932371d7 of JavaSMT in lib/java/runtime/.

  • java-smt:
    A checkout of JavaSMT in the version used in the submitted manuscript. It is a library and does not contain an executable application, except some examples. We provide it for documentation purpose.

  • sv-benchmarks:
    A subset of the sv-benchmark repository that contains all benchmarking tasks used in the evaluation.

  • packages:
    A set of deb-packages to be installed for running the evaluation. The packages are already installed in the provided virtual machine.

  • results:
    This directory contains the user’s result data after running an evaluation. The directory can be deleted and will be re-created when running a benchmark evaluation.

  • results_raw:
    The raw results from the evaluation at the time when writing the paper. Those results can be directly used for data analysis.

  • ARTIFACT_INFO.md:
    A short description of this artifact.

  • README.md:
    A description of how to use this artifact.

  • setup.sh: Commands for setting up the reproduction-package content, including which version of CPAchecker, JavaSMT, and SV-Benchmarks are downloaded and which changes are applied in the VM.

JavaSMT is updated regularly and new releases are published in Maven and Ivy containing bug fixes, new features, and the integration of new SMT solvers. We assume that the user might not want to develop an application based on this static reproduction package or within our virtual machine, but will directly use a proper IDE. Thus, we encourage the reader to directly visit the project web page: https://github.com/sosy-lab/java-smt
